entries.title: Days without spirits (손 없는 날)
entries.content: Koreans often move house on 'son eomneun nal': lunar days 9, 10, 19, 20, 29 and 30, when wandering spirits are said to be away. Moving companies charge more on these days.
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: The 12 day officers
entries.content: The almanac gives each day one of 12 'officers' (Establish, Remove, Full, Balance, Stable, Initiate, Destruction, Danger, Success, Receive, Open, Close). Each suits different tasks, like Open for starting or Destruction for clearing out.
entries.source: Skillon: Chinese Almanac and the 12 Day Officers
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: Picking a wedding date (택일)
entries.content: Families often ask a reader to pick a wedding day that combines well with both partners' charts and avoids clash days.
entries.source: Skillon: Marriage Date Selection; Korean custom
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: Ipchun posters (입춘대길)
entries.content: At the start of spring (about Feb 4), many homes post 'Ipchundaegil' (great luck at spring's start) on the door. This is also the day the saju year begins.
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: Your personal good days
entries.content: A good day for you is one whose animal combines with your day animal, or brings your Nobleman star. The Today tab checks this for you each day.
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection
